title: Spike sorting with Kilosort4
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Recover the times and unit assignments of injected ground-truth spikes from extracellular voltages, including no-drift hybrids and the full simulation drift conditions used in Figs. 3–4.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Recover the times and unit assignments of injected ground-truth spikes from extracellular voltages, including no-drift hybrids and the full simulation drift conditions used in Figs. 3–4.

Source-paper comparison for Original per-condition number/fraction of ground-truth units with matching score >0.8, with full score distributions and FP/FN companions: Paper unit score is 1−FP−FN: FP is unmatched detected spikes divided by detected spikes and FN is missed truth spikes divided by truth spikes, with matching tolerance ≤0.2 ms and the best of 40 closest detected units. Recovery is score>0.8. Released bench.py checks 20 and its nmatch may reuse an event; paper-faithful bookkeeping remains unresolved.
success_criteria: Recover publication-identical data, all registered paper obligations, original case denominators and Kilosort4 invocation before admitting a comparison.
Resolve paper40 versus released20 and event-matching semantics without selecting the favorable rule after seeing candidate results.

Beat both the authenticated published result and a competent author-baseline rerun on the same original cases, using a predeclared meaningful effect and uncertainty rule; retain all failures and false-positive companions.
Do not count a new simulation seed, a single hybrid, changed event assignment, narrowed unit subset or the local I_bijective_full policy as surpassing the paper.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
